what_its_for: Finasteride is used to treat two conditions in men: (1) Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH), which is an enlarged prostate gland that can make it hard to urinate — this is treated with the 5 mg dose (Proscar). (2) Male pattern hair loss (baldness on the top and front of the head) — this is treated with the 1 mg dose (Propecia). Finasteride works by lowering the amount of a hormone in your body called DHT (dihydrotestosterone) that causes the prostate to grow and hair follicles to shrink.
how_to_take: Take finasteride by mouth once a day, with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole — do not crush or break it. Try to take it at the same time every day to help you remember. Women and children should NEVER handle crushed or broken finasteride tablets, as the drug can be absorbed through the skin and cause serious harm, especially to unborn baby boys.
dosing: For enlarged prostate (BPH): The usual dose is 5 mg (Proscar) once daily. For male pattern hair loss: The usual dose is 1 mg (Propecia) once daily. Always take the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less than directed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — as long as it is still the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do NOT take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store finasteride at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, light, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep it in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medications out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medication down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Women who are pregnant or may become pregnant must NOT touch crushed or broken finasteride tablets. If a pregnant woman touches crushed tablets, she should wash the area with soap and water right away and call a doctor. Do not donate blood while taking finasteride and for at least 1 month after stopping it, because the drug in your blood could harm an unborn baby if given to a pregnant woman.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or seek medical help if you notice: breast lumps, pain, nipple discharge, or changes in breast tissue (these could be signs of a rare breast cancer in men); signs of a serious allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, or difficulty breathing; trouble urinating or not being able to urinate at all; pain or discomfort in the groin or pelvic area. Also talk to your doctor if you notice: decreased sex drive, trouble getting or keeping an erection, decreased amount of semen, or feelings of depression. These side effects can sometimes continue even after stopping the medication.
when_it_works: For enlarged prostate (BPH): You may start to feel improvement in urinary symptoms within a few weeks, but it may take 6 months or more to see the full benefit. For hair loss: You will need to take finasteride for at least 3 to 6 months before you notice any improvement. It may take up to 1 year to see the best results. Hair that was lost before starting the medication may not fully grow back. If you stop taking finasteride, any benefit you gained — whether for prostate or hair — will likely reverse within 6 to 12 months.
special_populations: Women and Children: Finasteride is NOT approved for use in women or children. Pregnant women must never handle crushed or broken tablets because the drug can be absorbed through skin and cause birth defects in male babies. Older Adults: Older men may use finasteride safely, but should still watch for any unusual side effects and report them to their doctor. Kidney or Liver Problems: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted or your doctor may monitor you more closely. PSA Testing: Finasteride can lower your PSA (Prostate-Specific Antigen) blood test results by about half. Always tell any doctor or lab technician that you are taking finasteride so they can correctly interpret your PSA results, which are used to screen for prostate cancer.
